title: Synaptic Analysis Workflow Using SEQUIN_v15 for Cortical Column Analysis
author: Andrew D Sauerbeck

steps.title: Initialize SEQUIN_v15 and Define Parameters
steps.instruction: Load the required Python packages and define the experimental input parameters.

substeps.instruction: Load all required Python packages defined in the code.
Define the input folder structure: a main 'Input Folder' containing 'Experimental image folder', 'Channel Alignment image folder', and 'Main output folder'.
Set the 'out_name' variable if rerunning analysis with different parameters.
Assign channel roles (sequin_reference, sequin_partner, or third_channel) using standard Python zero-based indexing.
Configure signal stability: use microscope auto brightness or set the 'z_intensity_correction_on' parameter.
Set 'percent_main' to select the percentage of spots for each channel based on brightness.
Set a predetermined correction value for non-specific background in the 'third_channel' if required.
Define intensity values and cutoffs for neurite labeling and masking.
Specify the maximum distance from a synaptic loci to search for a neurite.
Set multiple radii to test for parsing the 'third_channel' around synaptic loci.
Specify a maximum separation distance for synaptic pair analysis to save time.
Define background subtraction values for the reference, partner, and third_channel IDs.

steps.title: Perform Chromatic Aberration Correction
steps.instruction: Measure and correct for chromatic aberration using alignment images.

substeps.instruction: Use a subset of the brightest puncta (top 5% recommended) for measurement.
Specify the reference channel and the channel(s) to be aligned.
For three-channel imaging, use the fluorophore with the most central wavelength as the reference to minimize cropping effects.
Optionally omit XY chromatic aberration correction if magnitude is low.
Alternatively, apply known correction values to override the measurement step.

steps.title: Execute Core SEQUIN_v15 Processing
steps.instruction: Run the processing blocks to identify synaptic loci and perform measurements.

substeps.instruction: Run the parameter storage block of code.
Run the core code to load processing steps and perform chromatic aberration correction.
Set the number of simultaneous jobs based on computer resources.
Run the final block of code to perform SEQUIN analysis on the defined folders; outputs will be saved in the output folders.

steps.title: Apply LightGBM Model for Synaptic Identification
steps.instruction: Use a pre-trained LightGBM model to distinguish synaptic loci from non-synaptic pairs.

substeps.instruction: Load all required Python packages.
Define input folders (must be the output of SEQUIN_V15_step1) and output folders.
Define the output file name.
Specify the location and filename of the pre-trained model.
Run the parameter storage block.
Run the main block of code to save the output file.

steps.title: Process Tilescan Data (Optional)
steps.instruction: Simplify analysis of large tilescan imaging data using 'SEQUIN_V15_step3_process_tilescan_data.py'.

substeps.instruction: Load required Python packages.
Define the location of the master 'input_file_key' (matching example layout) and the output folder.
Define voxel spacing (e.g., set to 12 for Zeiss 980 in 8Y-SR-multiplex mode).
Optionally specify radial smoothing and tile subsamples (set radius to 0 and scaling factor to XY dimension for whole tile processing).
Crop final output data to user-defined areas and save representative images for confirmation.
Run the parameter storage block and then the analysis block.
Manually extract the resulting data from the 'density_psyn_correlation' variable (indices match input_key_file).

steps.title: Calculate Synaptic Density Around Masked Neurites
steps.instruction: Identify synaptic loci relative to neurite masks and calculate density.

substeps.instruction: Load required Python packages.
Define input/output folders, the original analysis image, and the neighbor cutoff for synaptic loci selection.
Specify intensity parameters for neurite masking.
Specify channel alignment values (must match SEQUIN_V15_step1).
Specify one or more radii to dilate neurites for density measurements.
Run the parameter storage block.
Run the core processing block (or skip and read previous output from a defined folder).
Recompile data by running the associated block.
Define the column to process from 'compiled_data' and the intensity binning interval.
Select the 'counts' column based on the dilation radius (Row 1) and whether synaptic loci inside the mask are 'raw' (included) or 'zeroed' (excluded) (Row 2).
Run the final block to store results in the 'all_data' variable.

steps.title: Reprocess Synaptic Loci Fields (Optional)
steps.instruction: Reprocess fields around synaptic loci to alter third-channel background subtraction or change field radius.

substeps.instruction: Load required Python packages.
Define input folders (Step 1 and Step 4 outputs) and the originally processed image.
Define the radius for parsing the third_channel.
Define channel alignment parameters (must match SEQUIN_V15_step1).
Run the first block of code, then the core processing block.
Optionally run the final block to bin data by distance from a labeled neurite, specifying bin start, interval, and number of bins.

steps.title: Adjust Tilescan Background Subtraction (Optional)
steps.instruction: Apply or change background subtraction for the third_channel in tilescan data.

substeps.instruction: Load required Python packages.
Define input/output folders, the originally processed image, and the maximum nearest neighbor distance for synaptic loci.
Define the channel for analysis and the background subtraction level.
Set the analysis radius around synaptic centroids.
Set neurite masking parameters and channel alignment parameters (must match initial processing).
Provide a 'tile_id_key' file containing Tile IDs to keep (obtained from the 'density_psyn_correlation' variable in Step 14).
Run the parameter storage block and the processing block.
Run the compilation block, specifying the column number for the current tilescan in 'tile_id_key' using zero-based indexing.

steps.title: Perform Cortical Column Analysis (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform correlation analysis within cortical columns using 'SEQUIN_V15_step7_cortical_column_analysis.py'.

substeps.instruction: Load required Python packages.
Define input/output folders and Airyscan settings (e.g., tile spacing of 12 for Zeiss LSM 980 8Y-Multiplex mode).
Set radius to 0 and scaling factor to 1 for full XY spatial resolution.
Run the code to generate heatmaps from processed SEQUIN data.
Define locations of cortical column reference maps and specify which rows in 'input_file_key' match each map.
Run the block to identify Secondary Motor Cortex Layer 2/3 and Layer 5 based on ROI IDs, using grayscale intensity values of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, or 60 to find up to six columns.
Run the final block to organize data into the 'current_data_x_pos_all' variable.
